messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Shreyash Pankaj
shreyash pankaj... that's a name that means business. where you working these days?
Juspay (Namma Yatri)

juspay... namma yatri! building the platform that's actually making autos work in bangalore. respect.

found shreyash pankaj on linkedin - SDE-1 at juspay, been there 2+ years scaling mobility. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/shreyaxh
Yes

sde at juspay for 2+ years, working on the mobility stack that's changing how india moves... from intern at incture to scaling namma yatri. solid progression. what made you stick around juspay this long? most people bounce after a year.
hey shreyash! was just thinking about your journey from incture to scaling namma yatri at juspay... what's making you stick around there for 2+ years when most people bounce after one?
There were plenty of learning opportunities for early career and every day was a new challenge so I was enjoying my time here at juspay. Also the comp was pretty competitive for fresher

User's LinkedIn Profile Context:
**EXECUTIVE SUMMARY**
Shreyash Pankaj is a backend and systems engineer currently employed at Namma Yatri. He is a 2023 graduate of UIET Panjab University.

**ROLE-BY-ROLE**
*   Namma Yatri (Date not specified) – [Role title not specified] – [Responsibilities not listed]

**EDUCATION HIGHLIGHTS**
*   UIET Panjab University (2019-2023) – [Degree not specified]

makes sense. juspay's one of those rare places where freshers actually get to touch real systems that millions use daily. plus good comp right out of college doesn't hurt. 

but here's the thing - you're 2+ years in now, not a fresher anymore. the learning curve's probably flattening, and your market value has definitely gone up since 2023. how long you been working total?
About 2years and 6 months

2.5 years... that sweet spot where you're not junior anymore but companies still see upside potential. the market's pretty good for backend engineers with your experience right now.

what kind of role you looking for next?
6 months more if you include internships

ah got it, so 2.5 total including the incture internship. that's solid experience for someone who graduated in 2023.

so what kind of role you looking for next?
3 years of you include the internship

right, 3 years total with the internship. that puts you in a much better bracket for roles.

so what kind of role you looking for next?
Backend/systems related roles for sde2 level

backend sde-2... smart move. 3 years at a fintech with real scale is perfect for that jump. most companies will see juspay experience as premium - you've dealt with payment systems, high throughput, the works.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Open to remote but prefer bangalore/pune/hyderabad only
3 years + backend/systems + sde-2 level + bangalore/pune/hyderabad... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Yupp sounds about right

yooo shreyash you're IN! 

welcome to the tal fam. you're officially on the radar now. no more scrolling through naukri looking at "urgent opening for passionate candidate" posts.

your profile's locked and loaded - 3 years backend experience, juspay fintech credibility, looking for that sde-2 jump in bangalore/pune/hyderabad. the algorithm knows what you want.

roles are gonna start flowing. when the right one hits, you'll know. till then, keep building cool stuff at juspay... but also keep your linkedin updated 😉
Sure thing look forward to it
Mostly growth, the work seems to have become repetitive. I want to use my skills to solve new problems

that's the real reason right there. hitting that plateau where you're good at what you do but the problems aren't new anymore. backend work gets stale when you're just maintaining vs building.

what kind of new problems you want to solve?
Definitely looking for a domain change. I have been working on namma yatri for a bit now so want to move out of the mobility domain

domain change makes total sense. mobility's cool but you've seen the patterns now. time for something new.

what domains are you curious about? fintech again but different? something completely different like gaming, AI infra, e-commerce?
Something completely new preferably. Open to anything honestly

open to anything is both exciting and dangerous. means you could end up somewhere amazing... or somewhere random.

what's your actual filter? like what would make you say "hell no" to a company?
Legacy systems, unstructured teams, toxic culture, too high work pressure

legacy systems, toxic culture, unstructured teams, high pressure... basically the four horsemen of the job search apocalypse. good filters.

what about comp? what's your current and what would make you move?

Currently at juspay i was making 21Lakhs as my base salary.

I currently have an offer from Fox Corporation where my base salary will be 35Lakhs + 2.625 Lakhs of bonus + 2.625 lakhs of equity annually

wait what

fox corporation? like the media company? that's a wild pivot from mobility to media. 35L base is solid though.

what's the role there? and are you actually considering it or just using it as leverage?

joining december 22nd... that's in two weeks. you're about to make a massive domain shift from indian mobility fintech to american media corporation.

what's making you still look around if you're seriously considering it? something feels off?
Its SDE2 backend. Rightnow i am seriously considering it, my joining date is 22 december
The company reviews on glassdoor and other career sites say that the company has a very toxic culture

ohhh there it is. 35L base but toxic culture warnings. classic tradeoff.

glassdoor reviews are usually right about culture. people don't make that shit up. toxic culture will make you hate that 35L real quick.

what specifically are the reviews saying?
Late night calls (us time zone), super tight deadlines, non supportive management

late night calls for US timezone, tight deadlines, unsupportive management... that's the exact toxic combo you said you wanted to avoid.

35L sounds nice until you're taking calls at 2am IST for some manager who doesn't care about your sleep schedule.

you're smart to keep looking. that fox offer is good leverage but sounds like a trap.
Exactly why I am still looking

smart move. you're using the fox offer as a benchmark but not letting desperation push you into another toxic situation.

what's your target comp range then? 35L base seems to be your new floor.
An offer in the same pay ramge with better culture

perfect. 35L+ base with actual good culture. that's the sweet spot.

location preference? remote okay or you want bangalore/pune/hyderabad?
Open to remote as well, fox is remote too

remote works. fox being remote sets the bar.

you're locked in my system now. i'll slide roles when i see something that actually fits - backend/systems sde-2, 35L+ base, good culture, remote or bangalore/pune/hyderabad.

btw what's your notice period at juspay?
18 December is my last working day, so i can join from 22december

got it. last day dec 18, can start dec 22. that's a tight window but doable for the right role.

i'll keep an eye out for something that beats the fox offer on culture while matching the comp. you're in the system now.

anything else you want me to know about what you're looking for?
Great, let me know if something suitable comes along

will do. i'll slide it right here when i see it.

good luck with the fox decision. remember: 35L isn't worth your mental health. you've got options.
Yupp, thanks

hey shreyash, was just thinking about your fox offer situation... 35L base but toxic culture warnings. that's a tough call.

curious - what would your ideal work culture actually look like? like if you could design it from scratch
Well i would prefer a hybrid work situation, flexible hours are preferred but not mandatory. Realistic deadlines so i don’t have to pull 10-12 hour work days

hybrid, flexible hours, realistic deadlines... basically the opposite of what fox reviews are saying.

makes sense. you want to actually enjoy the work, not just survive it.

what about team dynamics? like what kind of people would you want to work with?
Correct, work i can actually enjoy

that's the goal. work you can actually enjoy, not just endure.

so team dynamics - you want supportive management? collaborative peers? or more independent ownership?
Yeah sounds about right

cool. so hybrid/flexible, realistic deadlines, supportive management, collaborative peers... basically a place where you can do good work without burning out.

anything else you're looking for? like specific tech stack preferences or industries you want to avoid?
Not really, open to any modern tech stack. I come from haskell and servant background so would like to move out of it for sure

haskell and servant... that's niche. moving out makes sense - opens up way more opportunities.

modern tech stack means you're open to go, python, java, node, rust... basically anything that's not legacy.

what about the fox offer timeline? when do you need to decide by?
Well pretty soon i would say, by end of next week perhaps

end of next week... that's tight. but doable if something good comes along.

i'm keeping an eye out for roles that match your vibe - hybrid, flexible, good culture, modern stack. the moment i see something that beats fox on culture while matching comp, i'll slide it.

anything else i should know about what would make you jump?
Quality product, good comp, good people

quality product, good comp, good people. that's the trifecta.

fox has the comp, maybe the product... but the people/culture part seems shaky based on reviews.

i'll look for something that hits all three. you're in the system now.
Thanks

hey, saw a senior software engineer role at a D2C jewelry startup in pune

complete domain change from fintech to e-commerce, which you wanted

they mention user-first mindset and working directly with founders - could be the good culture you're looking for
Hey, tell me more about the company, the team size the tech stack product etc

the company is palmonas - a D2C jewelry brand. they're hiring through uplers (staffing agency).

tech stack is full-stack with backend focus: node.js, python, java for backend, react/vue for frontend. they mention ownership of features and working directly with founders.

team size isn't specified but it's a small startup vibe. product is jewelry e-commerce - think direct-to-consumer brand selling jewelry online.

the concern is it's a small D2C brand, not a tech-first company. could be high pressure with tight deadlines since it's e-commerce. also no salary info to verify if it hits your 35L+.

what's your take on small startups vs established companies?
I would prefer the stability and culture of established companies, have already worked in the startup vibe for 2+ years

that makes sense. after 2+ years in startup chaos, you want something more stable.

palmonas is definitely not that - small D2C brand, likely chaotic, no brand upgrade from juspay.

i'll keep looking for established companies with good culture. fox is established but culture seems toxic... need something that's both stable AND healthy.

anything specific about established companies you're looking for? like size, funding stage, industry?
Not really

got it. stable + good culture + 35L+ + backend/sde-2.

i'll filter out the startup chaos and find you something solid.
Sure thing

smart. wait for the offers, then compare comp, culture, and growth potential all at once.

keep me posted on what comes through. still keeping an eye out for anything that might beat all three.
Sure
I also have another offer from yipit data

wait what, that's three offers now? fox, commerceiq/e6data pending, and yipit data?

what's the yipit offer looking like? comp, role, location?

Comp: 27L base
Role: backend engineer (se2 equivalent)
Location: remote

27L base... that's 8L below your target minimum. remote is nice but that's a significant drop from what you're aiming for.

what's making you consider it?
Not considering it strongly anymore, got this offer before fox. But the culture and work quality is good

ah got it. so yipit has the culture and work quality but the comp is way off. fox has the comp but culture is questionable.

you're basically looking for the unicorn that has both. that's exactly what i'm scanning for.

any updates from commerceiq or e6data?
Not yet
got it. waiting game continues.

found a backend role in bangalore with 30-35L comp - exactly matches your fox offer

but it's through a staffing agency, so no clue about the actual company or culture

worth asking them which company it's for?
Sure let’s ask them
